title: Candidate read response (v2: no name)
description: A676 (interim, HIGH, privacy), PERD REQ-CTX-006 and REQ-AMB-002: at most 20 candidates, newest first (occurred_at descending; ties by candidate_id ascending, an agent rule so the order is total). JSON Schema cannot check the order; the reader and the Python test over fixtures do. NO NAME OF ANY KIND leaves the read: a candidate carries an opaque counterparty_ref (cp_1, cp_2, ... numbered in the answer's own order by first appearance of each normalised name, so the same counterparty gets the same one within this answer and nothing more: it groups counterparties within one candidate set, it is not a key and it is not derived from the name) and a recipient_match, the exact share of how well the name matched what the customer said (computed in core from the request's counterparty_surface; 0/1 when the request has none). An empty list is a valid answer and means NO_TRANSACTION_MATCH, never 'no such transfer happened' (REQ-AMB-002). A tenant mismatch is not a response: core returns 403 and raises a security event (REQ-CTX-006), and an out-of-scope row does not exist for the caller. v1 (counterparty_display) is not edited; its consumers move to this version.

Candidate.description: One candidate-shaped record: only the fields resolution features need (REQ-CTX-006) and no name of any kind (A676). The field list equals the candidates-api-shape lint's allowed names (plus v1's counterparty_display, allowed there only while v1 consumers exist); a test compares the two.

counterparty_ref.description: An opaque reference to the counterparty within this answer: cp_ and the ordinal of the counterparty's first appearance in the answer's own order (newest first, ties by candidate_id), the same normalised name getting the same one. It is not derived from the name, carries nothing of it, and means nothing outside this answer (no key, no hash, no source id).

recipient_match.description: How well the counterparty's name matched the counterparty the customer described (the request's counterparty_surface), as an exact share numerator/denominator in [0, 1], computed in core. 0/1 when the request carried no surface. The name itself never leaves core.

direction.description: OUTGOING or INCOMING, the two values the synthetic generator uses; no SoT or PERD value list exists (raised as an open decision).
